selectedComments.body:
🤖 **MFU pass 1: where the d512 step goes, and the first two fixes** (branch `ladderclimb_v1_batch14`)

**Profile** of the current best at d512 (`lc1-b24-prof`, steps 50–55, GPU 0). A step is **164 ms** of GPU time: 145 ms compute, 16 ms exposed NCCL, 3 ms idle. Model-FLOPs MFU is 10.4%.

The loop blocks on every step and then fetches about 300 metrics one D2H copy at a time, which costs about 40 ms of wall clock per step. That time falls **outside** the timed step window, so it doesn't count toward the 8-minute budget. Batching or thinning those fetches would still cut wall-clock cost.

I attributed each kernel to its JAX scope using the compiled HLO (new `--dump-hlo` launcher flag):

| component | ms / step | notes |
|---|---|---|
| NCCL (EP all-to-all SendRecv 27, all-gather 3) | 34 | 16 ms of it exposed |
| MoE expert MLP (fwd 17, bwd 20) | 37 | dispatch/combine selects on the [603k, 256] capacity buffers run at about 0.5 TB/s |
| MoE router / QB (fwd) | 12 | **router `lax.top_k` is a full XLA sort: 6 × 1.04 ms**; QB histogram scatter 2.2 ms |
| KDA (fwd 10, bwd 22) | 32 | Pallas kernels |
| fused CE loss | 12 | about 2.6× its GEMM floor: bf16 logits convert, one-hot select, max/sum passes |
| MLA + FA4 | 12 | |
| AttnRes gates | 10 | |
| GatedNorm / RMSNorm | 9 | |
| optimizer | ≈5 | cheap |

**Fixes in `3c229a7cb1`.** Neither changes the math; the smoke-test loss is bitwise equal.
1. **Router top-k** is now 9 unrolled max/argmax passes instead of `lax.top_k`. The indices are identical. H100 microbenchmark ([65536, 384] fp32, k = 9): **1.118 → 0.354 ms**. Expected saving: about 4.5 ms per step.
2. **Expert gate/up split** now indexes a `[..., 2, I]` view instead of `jnp.split`. The split's backward was a separate 617 MB concatenate of the two gradient halves. Microbenchmark of the pooled-wave expert MLP forward + backward at real shapes: **2.95 → 2.31 ms**, bitwise identical. Expected saving: about 4 ms per step. I made the same change in every EP backend through `split_moe_w13_output`.

A Pallas single-pass top-k crashed the process, and separate w1/w3 GEMMs were slower (3.08 ms), so I didn't use either.

| run | branch@commit | W&B | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ (paired) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MFU fixes, data-matched (same math: expect ≈ 3.0834, higher ex/s) | [`3c229a7cb1`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/3c229a7cb1) | [lc1-mfu1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-mfu1) | 2817 | 786 | | running | vs 3.0834 |
| + XLA default command-buffer set (FUSION, CUBLAS, CUBLASLT, CUSTOM_CALL, CUDNN; collectives eager), data-matched | [`3c229a7cb1`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/3c229a7cb1) | [lc1-cmdbuf-full](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-cmdbuf-full) | 2817 | | | running | vs 3.0834 |

A re-profile (`lc1-mfu1-prof`) will confirm the kernel savings. Next targets, in order:
- the dispatch/combine select fusions, about 12 ms at roughly 15% of HBM bandwidth
- the CE loss epilogue, about 5–7 ms
- the exposed EP all-to-all, 16 ms
- the QB histogram scatter, 2 ms

Every queued ladder run now also gets these speedups. Their losses are unaffected, and their ex/s will read higher than older runs'.

**Re-profile (`lc1-mfu1-prof`, same config at `3c229a7cb1`).** GPU span per step **164 → 154.5 ms (−5.8%)**, in line with the estimate. The host-timed step duration, which is what ex/s uses, has median **173.1 → 165.0 ms (−4.7%, +4.9% ex/s)** over steps 10–60, excluding the profiled window. That median comes from 60-step runs; `lc1-mfu1` will give the full-run number.

**Next lever: the host.** The host-timed step is about 10 ms longer than the GPU span. Inside `train_step`, 9.3 ms pass between the call starting and the first kernel running: `ParseArguments` takes 6 ms to flatten the state pytree, and the loop blocks on the loss every step, so the GPU drains in the meantime. The host call then returns 3 ms *after* the GPU finishes, because the host spends the entire step inside `ExecuteThunks`. It launches 3345 kernels plus 848 D2D copies per step, with command buffers disabled. The GPU is barely ahead of the host, so further kernel work could stop paying off unless launches get cheaper.

Command buffers were turned off for the CUDA-graph hang in #5675. The later bisection there pins the hang on the **collectives** capture set. XLA's default set (fusion, cuBLAS, cuDNN, custom calls, with collectives left eager) ran hang-free and gave +2.1% on GB200. `lc1-cmdbuf-prof` tests that set here. If it holds, I'll also pipeline the loop so step N+1 is dispatched before blocking on step N.


**Command buffers (`lc1-cmdbuf-prof`, 60 steps, env `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=FUSION,CUBLAS,CUBLASLT,CUSTOM_CALL,CUDNN`).**
- **Step time:** the median host-timed step goes **165.0 → 160.0 ms (−3.0%)**. The host gap closes: the timed step now about equals the GPU span, because launches go out as graphs.
- **Exposed communication:** it rises from 16 to 20–22 ms. With the collectives running eagerly between graphs, some overlap is lost.
- **Loss:** step-59 loss is 4.6178 vs 4.6158.
- **One stall:** one profiled step stalled for 577 ms.

`lc1-cmdbuf-full` (2817 steps, with eval) checks for hangs and full-run throughput before I make this the fast_track default.

sources.title: [grug] Add the Hero H100 pipeline prototype
[iris] Group JAX GPU startup and detect divergent compiles
sources.body:
Group Iris's JAX startup code under `iris.jax`: the multi-process GPU hook and supervisor, compilation and autotune cache setup, distributed initialization, and compile guard. Levanter, Fray, Grug, and Iris callers use the new entrypoints. The supervisor launches children before they import JAX. `initialize_jax()` configures caches before joining the distributed world and installs the guard after multi-process GPU initialization.

Before a multi-process GPU compile enters native XLA, the guard compares JAX compile keys across participating processes. Mismatched keys raise with each process index and observed key; a missing peer fails after 60 seconds. On `origin/main` at `054142676a`, a two-host H100 probe with a rank-dependent constant left one rank in `ConfigAssigner::AssignConfigs`, while the matching control compiled on both. With the guard, divergent probes failed promptly and matching probes succeeded on JAX 0.11.0 and 0.11.1. The [issue research comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9042#issuecomment-5789182658), [JAX 0.11.0 divergent run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fissue-9042-pipeline-divergent-20260922), and [JAX 0.11.0 control](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fissue-9042-pipeline-control-20260922) contain the evidence. The 67B Snowball train step was not rerun.

The guard compares JAX's pre-compile key; differences introduced only inside native XLA remain outside its coverage. Focused Iris, Levanter, and Fray tests passed (140). The safe affected suite had 5,132 passes, 7 skips, 6 expected failures, and two Tasktrove/Zephyr 30-second timeouts; both timed-out tests passed in isolation. Repository lint and type checking passed.

Part of #9042

[grug] Resume Hero pipeline checkpoints
sources.body:
Save and resume Hero pipeline model parameters, optimizer state, and pending QB router updates through Levanter's completed `step-N` checkpoints. The stage-independent tree uses global layer paths and restores into the compiled MPMD placement, including pinned-host optimizer state; unused compiled input leaves retain their initialized placement so saved values remain representable. `--steps` remains the total training schedule length across restarts.

CPU round trips for AdamW and MuonH pass with a changed stage split; the focused Hero and original Grug pipeline tests have 16 passes and one skip. The affected safe suite has 2,198 passes, four skips, five expected failures, and eight macOS loopback failures independently reproduced on the base branch and addressed separately in #9442.

On two H100x8 nodes, a reduced-width four-layer pipeline saved step 1, restored it, and completed step 2. Resumed step-2 loss was 6.94263744 versus 6.94263697 in an uninterrupted control (absolute difference 4.77e-7). A separate two-layer, full-width Hero probe (d6144, 384 experts) at sequence length 4096 also saved step 1 and resumed through step 2. Resumed step-2 loss was 11.56717205 versus 11.56716919 in its uninterrupted control (absolute difference 2.86e-6). All six save, resume, and control jobs completed with finite losses and both Iris and native worker exits at zero. Both configurations used PP2, EP8, BF16 MuonH, and pinned-host optimizer state. Checkpoints were written only to scratch storage.

These are bounded checks; the full 48-layer, 65K-token Hero training shape has not been checkpointed and resumed. The GPU probes used the pinned JAXPP build plus local offload and DIME patches required by the Hero pipeline; durable upstream support remains a dependency of #9279. Existing Hero FSDP checkpoints have a different stacked state tree with optional master and EMA weights and are not importable by this runner. Stacked on #9279.

sources.title: [iris] Allow 30 minutes for GPU compile rendezvous
sources.body: Allow distributed GPU ranks up to 30 minutes to reach the compile-fingerprint rendezvous. A 67B checkpoint load reached the same compile fingerprint on every rank, but one rank arrived about 72 seconds after the others and tripped the former 60-second limit. The guard still rejects missing or divergent ranks.
